title: Linux_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_415
description: Investigate and identify malicious activity, determine its scope, and recommend containment measures for the Linux/Remaiten botnet.
outcomes: Usage of systemctl for service management
Systemd timer investigation for persistence mechanisms

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential unauthorized access. Your task is to investigate and identify any malicious activity related to the Linux/Remaiten botnet family, determine its scope, and recommend containment measures.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Host: victim (192.168.80.100)
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service that is periodically communicating with an external host? The flag is the name of the service.
levels.solution: Check running services and their network connections. Look for services that connect to external hosts on non-standard ports. The flag is 'bot-beacon.service'.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by listing all running services to identify any unusual or unauthorized services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all running services. Look for a service named 'bot-beacon.service'.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The service you are looking for is named 'bot-beacon.service'. Use the command 'systemctl status bot-beacon.service' to check its status and network connections.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service generating abnormal volumes of network traffic? The flag is the name of the service.
levels.solution: Investigate network connections and look for services sending multiple requests to the same destination. The flag is 'bot-flood.service'.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate network connections to identify services generating abnormal traffic.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'ss -tulnp' to list all network connections. Look for a service named 'bot-flood.service'.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The service you are looking for is named 'bot-flood.service'. Use the command 'ss -tulnp | grep bot-flood.service' to verify its network connections.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the name of the systemd timer responsible for the persistence of the suspicious service? The flag is the name of the timer.
levels.solution: Check systemd timers and services that might be related to the suspicious service identified in previous tasks. The flag is 'system-update-checker.timer'.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers to determine how the suspicious service persists after reboot.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-timers' to list all systemd timers. Look for a timer named 'system-update-checker.timer'.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The timer you are looking for is named 'system-update-checker.timer'. Use the command 'systemctl status system-update-checker.timer' to check its status and related services.
